html:
A Japanese poet of the early Tokugawa period who made the short verse later called haiku into a serious art. He is the most famous poet in Japanese.

Born near Ueno in Iga province to a family of low samurai rank, he served a young lord who shared his love of verse. He later moved to Edo and became a teacher of linked verse, a social game in which poets took turns adding lines. The opening verse of such a chain, the hokku, became his special form. His pupils planted a banana tree, a bashō, by his hut, and he took its name.

His best known poem tells of an old pond and the sound of a frog jumping in. His poems join plain, everyday images with a sense of loneliness and passing time, shaped by his study of Zen.

He spent his last ten years largely on foot. His journey of 1689 into the far north became The Narrow Road to the Deep North, a mix of prose and poems. He died on a journey in Osaka in 1694.
sum: A Japanese poet of the early Tokugawa period who made the short verse later called haiku into a serious art. He is the most famous poet in Japanese.
